verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "it's been happening for about, three days now" referring to diarrhea.
Doctor: "how many times a day are you going to the toilet?" Patient: "Uh, four to five." Doctor clarifies this is diarrhea and discusses watery vs loose stools, indicating loose/watery consistency.
Patient: "it's pretty standard diarrhoea, where it's was like a little bit of abdominal pain." This supports intermittent mild abdominal pain.
Patient: "I threw up once, that was a little worrying" and repeats "I threw up once, yeah."
Doctor: "Any fever at all?" Patient: "Uh, maybe a little bit, but... it hasn't been, that in particular hasn't been too worrying." This supports a possible low-grade fever.
Patient: "Appetite loss I guess worse than normal" and confirms still drinking: Doctor: "you're still able to drink quite a bit yeah?" Patient: "Yeah yeah yeah."
Doctor: "is there any blood or mucus?" Patient: "No blood" and later "No" to mucus. Doctor: "No, so no mucus, OK."
Patient: "nothing funky in my diet and no travels recently" and Doctor confirms "So you haven't had anything from outside? Nothing dodgy" with patient denying.
Doctor: "what have you take, have you taken anything so far for the diarrhea?" Patient: "Nothing yet." Doctor: "Anything for the abdominal pain?" Patient: "Uh, nothing yet."
Patient: "Probably I I had asthma... or, or I don't know I guess I still have it."

Doctor asks about inhalers; Patient: "Lexapro" / "Laxepro"; Doctor: "Is it like Salbutamol? Is it like a blue colour?" Patient: "Yellow." Doctor: "Yellow, OK. I'll have to check that one, not sure. Laxepro." This supports a yellow inhaler called 'Laxepro' with details unknown.
Doctor: "Any allergies?" Patient: "No... Nothing, yeah, nothing." Doctor: "No allergies at all."
Patient: "my dad had hypertension... Has hypertension. Had hypertension. Yeah he died of bowel cancer ten years ago." Doctor: "And how old was he when he died?" Patient: "Uh, sixty-two."
Doctor, observing via video: "you're still drinking plenty and you look like you're not dehydrated which is a good sign." This implies patient appears well without overt dehydration.
The transcript describes diarrhea history and advice but does not state a formal diagnosis such as "acute self-limited infectious gastroenteritis" or label severity as mild.

Doctor: "You still need to drink plenty of water because you're losing a lot of fluids" and later: "you could get something called Dioralyte over the counter. So, it helps to uh, replenish your, the salts that you've been, that's lost through going to the toilet." This supports increased fluids and ORS use with loose stools.

Doctor advises avoiding certain foods while having diarrhea and reintroducing after 48 hours without diarrhea: "avoid dairy, fish, meat, eggs, while you're having the diarrhea" and "Forty-eight hours you're not having any diarrhea, you're fine then you can go and start having meat, egg, fish and all." The fact incorrectly says avoid for at least 48 hours after the last loose stool, which reverses the timing.
Doctor: "although you can't milk is not a good idea, yoghurts are a good idea because they are probiotics, it help to build up the normal, um gut, gut bacteria back."
Doctor notes patient has taken nothing for pain but does not explicitly state "No medications required currently" or recommend "simple analgesia as needed" for abdominal pain.

Doctor provides red-flag advice: "if your diarrhoea doesn't go away in a week's time, or if you're passing blood, we need a stool sample" and "If you're... going about six to eight times a day... you might need to go into hospital... If that happens you get in touch with us again." This reflects education on red flags and actions.
